digest.component_or_area: completion verification harness (production in-process vs external agent)
propositions: Production in-process verifier (Arm A) achieved 100% per-AC agreement on 65 judgments with zero false-PASS on planted ACs, while minimal external harness agent (Arm B) achieved 94.6% on 92 judgments (5 false-FAIL on real epic ACs, zero false-PASS on planted).

Arm A's claimed unreliability from in-process scaffolding (step budget, structured tool surface, output contract) was not observed in control transcripts or new runs; guanaco's known 2 agentic false-FAILs and 35-55 step variance did not reproduce.

Arm B's 5 false-FAIL verdicts concentrated on 0e68-real epic AC7 (stamp/mapping mutation commit claim) and AC2 (enrichment data assertion), representing strict-literal strict readings of coverage gaps rather than harness constraint failures.

Arm B produced zero INSUFFICIENT verdicts by treating external-ish AC claims (Gerrit change pushed, plan comment recorded) as in-tree-verifiable via tickets-branch citations, contrary to the insufficiency-loop pain hypothesis.
Production verifier median wall time 131 s vs external agent 415.5 s (3× slower, failing the ≤2× rule) due to task-agent overhead including full test-suite execution (20-43 min incl. lint/typecheck).

Predeclared GO conditions: (i) false-PASS=0 for both (HOLDS), (ii) Arm B rejections 5 strictly < Arm A rejections 0 (FAILS: 5 < 0 is false), (iii) Arm B median 415.5 ≤ 262 s (FAILS); result NO-GO — production verifier superior on accuracy and speed; external-harness seam not justified; actionable residue is 0e68 AC7/AC2 coverage gaps only.
